auditor_value: a₂ = 2g(2η − sinθ)/(4η + 1); positive means m₂ accelerates downward (m₂ goes up when 2η < sinθ)

findings.quote: the two upward pulls from cord 2 must together balance the one downward pull from cord 1
findings.note: Directions reversed for the served figure. Cord 1 comes down from the corner pulley to the axle and holds the hanging pulley UP (T₁ upward); cord 2 passes over the top of the hanging pulley with both segments running downward, so its two tensions pull the pulley DOWN (2T₂ downward). The printed equation T₁ = 2T₂ is right; the reason given for it is false.
findings.fix: The hanging pulley is massless, so the single upward pull T₁ from cord 1 at its axle must balance the two downward pulls T₂ from the segments of cord 2.

findings.quote: the second cord loops under the movable pulley with one end fixed and one end on m2
findings.note: The served figure says the second cord passes over the TOP of the hanging pulley and both of its segments run downward to the bracket and to m₂. 'Loops under' describes a different arrangement (a pulley hanging in a loop), which is not the one drawn.
findings.fix: the second cord passes over the top of the hanging pulley; one segment runs down to the fixed bracket and the other runs down to m2

findings.note: Unconditional. The expression 2g(2η − sinθ)/(1 + 4η) is negative when 2η < sinθ, in which case m₂ accelerates upward and m₁ slides down the incline; the sign of the result carries the direction.
findings.fix: directed downward when 2η > sinθ; when 2η < sinθ the expression is negative and m₂ accelerates upward

question_defect: The question never states that the wedge is fixed, and says every surface is frictionless; with no wedge mass given, the only workable reading is a fixed wedge, which the solution assumes without saying so.
notes: Independently: constraint a₂ = 2a₁ (m₁ up the incline by x lowers the hanging pulley by x and lengthens the m₂ segment by x); T₁ = 2T₂; T₁ − m₁g sinθ = m₁a₁; ηm₁g − T₂ = ηm₁(2a₁); gives a₁ = g(2η − sinθ)/(1 + 4η) and a₂ = 2a₁. Every printed equation follows. The single common_mistakes entry reproduces its stated denominator (1 + 2η) when a₂ = a₁ is used with T₁ = 2T₂.
